summary: Feed s148_double is degraded: NDR port overloaded by 24.66 Gbps bursts (247% of 10 Gbps capacity) causing 2.5% TCP packet loss. Duplicates, VLANs, encryption share and directionality are healthy, but overload-induced drops break NDR full-payload analysis.

findings.root_cause: Peak burst of 24.66 Gbps in 1 ms interval exceeds the NDR's 10 Gbps port capacity by 247% (metric 2.466 vs 0.8 threshold). Packet broker forwards aggregate traffic to single tool port without load balancing, causing buffer overrun and ingress drops.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR drops packets at ingress, misses flows and payload segments, degrades detection coverage and causes false negatives; violates NDR requirement for complete bidirectional full-payload visibility.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute bursts across 3x10G tool ports with flow-aware 5-tuple hashing to keep per-port utilization <80% while preserving both directions per flow for NDR stateful analysis.

findings.root_cause: 200 of 8061 TCP packets (2.48% vs 1% threshold) show gaps/retransmissions indicating loss in SPAN/mirror or packet broker buffers, exacerbated by the 24.66 Gbps overload bursts.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR receives incomplete TCP streams, breaks stream reassembly and signature matching requiring full payload, reducing detection fidelity and increasing missed detections.

recommended_fix.why: Replace lossy SPAN/mirror with passive TAP for lossless line-rate copy to eliminate SPAN buffer drops; combined with load balancing ensures complete packets reach NDR without loss.
